title: Committed Python bytecode artifact tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc — build cache tracked in git and not ignored
evidence:
diff --git a/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc b/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f807a4d
Binary files /dev/null and b/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc differ
--- repo check: `git ls-files tools/__pycache__` lists the .pyc; `git check-ignore` prints NOT-IGNORED; .gitignore has no pycache/pyc entry.
detail: A CPython bytecode cache is a machine-generated build artifact. Every local run of the derivation script will dirty it (or diverge from it), creating PR churn and a stale duplicate of the derivation logic.
recommended_fix: git rm --cached the .pyc and add `__pycache__/` (or `*.pyc`) to .gitignore.

title: CI gate 2 label still reads 'Core unit tests' but the command now runs five suites plus a 3x repeat loop
evidence: "Core unit tests (the determinism + topology contracts)|mkdir -p bin && odin test core && for i in 1 2 3; do odin test app -out:bin/app-test || exit 1; done && odin test app/render -out:bin/render-test && odin test app/audio -out:bin/audio-test && odin test harness -out:bin/harness-test"
detail: The gate label is the human-facing CI step name and the file header claims 'One entry per GH CI run step... parity by construction'. The label no longer describes the content, misleading future gate maintenance.
recommended_fix: Rename the label to reflect the full suite, e.g. "Unit tests (core + app + render + audio + harness, app 3x repeat)".

title: palcheck's map-vs-signal threshold discrimination re-derives pair classification by color-value comparison while the derivation script uses labeled pairs — the twins can drift
detail: The Python twin tags each pair ('map-water-park', T_MAP) at construction; palcheck instead inspects pr[0]'s color value. If a signal token ever shares a color with a map token, or pair construction reorders, the threshold silently misclassifies.
recommended_fix: Carry a per-pair threshold (or a map/signal tag) in the pairs array at append time, mirroring the script's labeled construction.
